emergency.t: LANE A / LANE B Warning Light

s.n: The Lane warning lights can flash or be permanently illuminated depending on the nature of the fault. If a warning indicator remains on permanently, an error of higher severity (Failure) has been detected by the ECU internal tests. The ECU continues to operate in an alternative control mode, transferring control of ignition and injection to the error-free Lane. Both regular and alternative modes can deliver full engine power; the engine is operated in power-mode with increased fuel consumption.
Refer to Rotax Operator and Maintenance Manuals for troubleshooting.

s.a: Switch OFF non-essential electrical loads (Strobe lights OFF)

s.n: The ECU System requires an electrical power source for its operation. If one alternator fails, continued engine operation is assured by the other alternator. Therefore, the airframe loads are supplied by battery.
Detected by LOW VOLT warning light, ESS VOLT CAS message and positive battery ammeter. With Generator A failure, Lane A and Lane B warning lights flash.

s.a: Switch OFF non-essential electrical loads (Pitot Heat and Strobe lights OFF)

s.n: In case of failure of the remaining generator expect imminent engine stoppage.

If any generator fails, the airframe electrical system is automatically cut off from the generator. The battery is the remaining source for the airframe electrical system for a minimum of 30 minutes. Additional load shedding, according to flight conditions, could extend battery capacity.

The BCK BATT switch is required to be set ON during in-flight engine restart and in case of both alternators failure. The BCK BATT light is illuminated when the switch is ON; the ECU system is then powered by the aircraft battery.
Recognized by simultaneous loss of: PITOT HEAT, PFD, EIS, COM 1, ADAHRS, NAV1/GPS, ANNUNC PANEL, LND LIGHT, BUFF BATTERY, G3X POWER 2, STROBE LIGHT, STALL, FLAP, GDA 29, GMU.

Change or maintain flight conditions according to available equipment. Refer to standby instrument for primary flight information. Audio panel is usable via MFD. Strobe and landing lights are lost; NAV and taxi lights are still available.
Recognized by simultaneous loss of: AUDIO PANEL, XPDR, NAV LIGHT, TAXI LIGHT, SOCKET 12V, STDBY INSTR, INT LIGHT, PITCH TRIM.

Fail-safe operation of G3X Touch allows pilot to transmit and use COM1 using headphones only; speakers will not be available. For night flights all instruments and map lights are lost, but emergency light is still available.
Recognized by loss of MFD.
